entry_points.text: Table builder is the init entry under held enablement and stable CPU set; it returns success after full construction and negative status on failure without partial publication.
Override is the init-time extension entry in a filtered set restricted to identity-init context; outside it or without a live scheduler it only reports an error.

Translation and topology query are steady-state entries resolving caller program to scheduler; module init registers helpers and slice and bypass intervals expose clamped setters with unsigned getters.

exports.text: Build dense identity tables from online topology, allow init-time layout override, and provide steady-state translation plus topology query.
Mutate caller masks over declared intervals with clear and fill, query with subset and empty, and fold or extract via reference helpers.
Centralize range checks for identities and CPUs, combine validation with lookup reporting errors, and pass through non-identity values.
Register identity helpers in an init-filtered set and a general set, initializing them across complementary program categories in sequence.
Claim scheduler exit with formatted message and metadata, test ancestry by level and ancestor slot, and resolve node-local and user queues.
Open, release, reacquire and close traversal over scheduler tasks in global list mode or cgroup descendant mode.

hazards.text: Extension counts and arrays are snapshotted before validation and shared mask words use ordered access, so checks and install see stable copies.
CPUs without node info defer to the ungrouped tail; domains without cache info fall back to node grouping with a warning; affected CPUs still get valid identities.
All replacement failures report through the scheduler error channel and return before any table write, so observers see the prior or the fully new layout.
Predicate walks stop at the deciding word while mutating walks visit all overlap; empty intervals bypass access; undersized shard extraction forces empty at the shard base with an error.
Backtrace capture is skipped in NMI context and the abort sweep uses lockless ordered marks plus deferred work; undersized init truncates and oversize reframe keeps prior state with warnings.
Exhaustion reports ENOMEM and bad arguments EINVAL as negative status; absent NUMA uses the NO_NODE marker; slice and bypass ranges plus initial cursor and dump-CPU defaults are fixed.
Behavior relies on opaque external helpers for ordered access, guards, CPU and node masks, lists and BPF registration; internals are outside this dossier.

invariants.text: Identities form a dense sequence covering all possible CPUs; forward and reverse tables are mutual inverses; bad override input leaves tables unchanged.
Shards partition identities into ordered non-overlapping intervals within a capped size; base, count, home node and total count rebuild on layout change.
Online CPUs record shard, core, cache-domain and node membership with representative plus ordinal; unknown levels use a negative marker.
Mask walks touch only intersecting words with edge masking and preserve outside bits; empty overlap skips access; init clamps and reframe rejects oversize.
Subset fails if any set bit lies outside the container span; emptiness means no set bit in span; iteration yields set positions in word order.
Program-to-scheduler resolution returns null for dead or unassociated schedulers, preferring associated ops then global root with legacy compat.
Validated references snapshot start, count, capacity and shard span rejecting overruns; home node is strict majority; sequence uses signed-difference order.
Queue traversal skips BPF cursor markers until head repeats; only three reserved ids are runqueue-owned; bypass enqueue climbs to nearest non-bypassing scheduler.
At load the extension reports disabled and unswitched; runqueue handover clears source tracking, swaps locks, then tracks the destination.

locks.text: Construction requires stable online CPU set and exclusive enablement and runs pre-publication with blocking allocation.
Replacement runs under enablement exclusion while unpublished and inside a read-side section; blocking copies occur before entering it.
Translation and topology query use a read-side section without mutation; missing scheduler or tables yields an error.
Traversal, cursor advance, openness checks and runqueue switching require respective locks held; task iteration uses a dedicated list lock; exit claim uses preemption and read-side guards.

state_machines.text: Construction allocates and fills sentinels, assigns online CPUs grouped by node, cache and core with bounded splits, packs the remainder, warns on degraded topology, then derives ranges and publishes count.

Replacement snapshots extension arrays under bounds, validates counts, order, spans, range and uniqueness, then installs translations, derives majority home nodes, resets topology except shards, and rebuilds ranges.
Exit moves from none to a concrete kind exactly once; parent kinds mark local abort while others abort the subtree, emit a trace, record message and metadata, then queue disable work.
Openness orders by class relative to the extension class, then dispatch nesting, then preempt flag with protected-slice veto, else closed when an extension task occupies the runqueue.
Cursor skips newer entries, repositions beside the returned task or detaches at end; iteration starts in cgroup or list mode, unlocks, and removes the cursor on stop.

structs.text: Per-identity topology record carries shard, core, cache-domain and node pairs of representative plus ordinal; negative denotes unknown.
Mask header gives base, count, word storage and capacity; validated reference adds scheduler, source and shard span with empty intervals collapsed.
Table collection holds forward and reverse translation, per-identity shard and topology, per-shard home node and ranges plus count; unmapped reverse entries use a negative sentinel.
Global state keeps RCU root, scheduler and task hashes, enable mutex and sequence, cgroup flag, task and scheduler cursors and watchdog interval.
Per-CPU state holds locked runqueue, direct-dispatch task, kick-sync pointers and identifier cursors; dispatch iterator and hashes keyed by cgroup, task and queue ids.

Masks use 64-bit words with an 8192 CPU ceiling and -1 unmapped sentinel; shard size has a default capped by a maximum; predicate, mutating and ordered op kinds are separated; reverse, slice and vtime use bits 16, 30 and 31.
